title: The Past Simple
summary: The *būtasis kartinis laikas*: one past tense doing the work of the English simple past, perfect and continuous together. It has two sets of endings, and which of them a verb takes is settled by the third form given in the dictionary.

rules.heading: The Third Principal Part
rules.statement: Every Lithuanian verb is cited with **three** forms — *dirbti, dirba, dirbo* — and the third of them is the past. It is not derivable from the other two, which is exactly why the dictionary gives it: the past stem must be learnt with the verb, as the present stem was (¶35). Once it is known, the whole tense follows, because the past has only **two** patterns of ending against the present's three.

paradigms.caption: The three principal parts
paradigms.footnote: The present type and the past type are independent: *valgyti* is a third-conjugation present and an *-ė* past, *kalbėti* a second-conjugation present and an *-o* past. Knowing one tells you nothing about the other.

rules.heading: The Past of the -o Type
rules.statement: Where the third principal part ends in **-o**, the personal endings are those below. Cut the *-o* from the cited form and add them; the third person is the cited form itself, and serves both numbers as it does in the present (¶57).

paradigms.caption: dirbti, dirba, dirbo — past
paradigms.footnote: So too *ėjau, ėjai, ėjo, ėjome, ėjote, ėjo* and *kalbėjau, kalbėjai, kalbėjo, kalbėjome, kalbėjote, kalbėjo*.

examples.gloss: Last year we lived in Kaunas.
Did you speak to the teacher?

rules.heading: The Past of the -ė Type
rules.statement: Where the third principal part ends in **-ė**, the endings differ in the first and second person singular: **-iau** and **-ei**. The *-iau* is a back vowel, and it therefore softens a preceding **t** to *č* and **d** to *dž*, exactly as the genitive does (¶28) — *skaitė* gives *skaičiau*, not *skaitiau*.

paradigms.caption: skaityti, skaito, skaitė — past
paradigms.footnote: Likewise *matė → mačiau*, *valgė → valgiau*, *rašė → rašiau*. The softening happens only before *-iau*; the other five forms keep the consonant unaltered.

rules.heading: The Past of Būti
rules.statement: **Būti** is regular in the past, whatever it does in the present: its third principal part is *buvo*, and the *-o* endings of ¶94 apply without exception. Note that where the present tense may drop *yra* altogether (¶16), the past may **not** — *buvo* has to be said.

examples.note: the predicate noun stands in the nominative, as in the present (¶16)

rules.heading: Negation in the Past
rules.statement: Negation works in the past exactly as in the present: **ne-** is written onto the front of the verb as one word (¶25), and the object of the negated verb goes into the **genitive** (¶26). Nothing about the past tense alters either rule — which is worth stating plainly, because learners commonly keep the accusative once the sentence moves out of the present.

examples.gloss: She did not read the book.

rules.heading: Telling What Happened
rules.statement: The one past tense covers what English divides among three: *dirbau* is *I worked*, *I was working* and *I have worked* alike, and the context or an adverb supplies the difference. The adverbs that most often supply it are **vakar** (yesterday), **pernai** (last year) and **prieš** with the accusative (¶87). This is also the tense of a biography — where one was born, where one studied, where one worked.

rows.label: continuous
cells: When you rang, I was working.

rows.label: perfect
cells: I have already worked in Lithuania.

examples.target: Studijavau universitete, o paskui dirbau mokykloje.
examples.gloss: I studied at the university, and afterwards worked at a school.
A year ago I came to Lithuania.

drills.stem: **dirbti, dirba, dirbo.** What is *I worked*?
drills.explanation: Third part *dirbo* → *-o* past → 1sg **dirbau**. *dirbu* present; *dirbo* 3rd; *dirbome* 1pl.

drills.stem: Complete: **Vakar ____ namie.** (Yesterday I was at home.)
drills.explanation: *būti* past is regular *-o*: *buvau*. Unlike present *yra*, past *buvo/buvau* must be said (¶96).

drills.stem: **skaityti, skaito, skaitė.** What is *I read* (past)?
drills.explanation: *-ė* past → 1sg **-iau**, and *t* softens to *č*: **skaičiau**. *skaitiau* without softening is the near-miss; *skaitau* is present.

drills.stem: Which are **past** forms?
drills.explanation: *mačiau* (*matė*) and *valgėme* (*valgė*) are past; *matau*/*gyvena* present. Softening in *mačiau* marks *-iau*.

drills.stem: Complete: **Ji neskaitė ____.** (She did not read the book.)
drills.explanation: Negated verb → object in **genitive**, past unchanged: *knygos*. Keeping accusative *knygą* after *ne-* is the classic slip (¶97).

drills.stem: Why can *dirbau* be three English tenses at once?
options: Because it is ambiguous between persons.
Because Lithuanian has one past where English splits simple, continuous and perfect.
Because it may also be present.
drills.explanation: *I worked / was working / have worked* are all *dirbau*; adverbs supply the nuance (¶98).

drills.stem: Which statements about the past are correct?
options: The third person serves both singular and plural.
There are two ending sets, *-o* and *-ė*.
Past type is predictable from present conjugation.
Negation is written onto the verb as one word.
drills.explanation: Present type ≠ past type: *valgyti* is 3rd-conj present + *-ė* past; *kalbėti* 2nd-conj present + *-o* past — hence three dictionary forms (¶93).

drills.stem: **rašyti, rašo, rašė.** Second person singular past?
drills.explanation: *-ė* past → 2sg **-ei**: *rašei*. *rašai* present; *rašiau* 1sg past; *rašėte* 2pl.

drills.stem: **Jis buvo mokytojas.** Why not accusative *mokytoją*?
options: Because a predicate noun after *būti* stands in the nominative, past as present.
Because the past tense governs the nominative.
drills.explanation: *būti* links, not governs — predicate nominative (¶16 / ¶96). Tense changes nothing.

drills.stem: Which 1sg past forms correctly show **consonant softening** before *-iau*?
drills.explanation: *t→č* and *d→dž* before *-iau*. *valgiau* keeps *g*; *dirbau* is *-o* type with no softening (¶95).

drills.stem: How many **distinct written forms** does a Lithuanian verb have in the past across all six persons?
drills.explanation: Five: 3rd person is one form for both numbers — *dirbau, dirbai, dirbo, dirbome, dirbote* (¶94 / ¶57).

drills.stem: **Vakar skaičiau gerą knygą.** Negated: how many of the four words change form?
drills.explanation: Three: *skaičiau*→*neskaičiau*, *gerą*→*geros*, *knygą*→*knygos*. *Vakar* is untouched. Negation pulls both adjective and noun into the genitive (¶97).

drills.stem: **gyventi, gyvena, gyveno.** What is *we lived*?
drills.explanation: *-o* past → 1pl **-ome**: *gyvenome* (¶94).

drills.stem: **matyti, mato, matė.** What is *I saw*?
drills.explanation: *-ė* past → 1sg **-iau** with *t*→*č*: *mačiau* (¶95).

drills.stem: Past 1sg of **būti**?
drills.explanation: *buvo* + *-o* endings → *buvau* (¶96).

drills.stem: Complete: **Vakar ____ namie.** (Yesterday I was at home.)
drills.explanation: Past of *būti*: *buvau* (¶96). *buvo* is 3rd person.

drills.stem: Complete: **Ji ____.** (She did not read the book.)
drills.explanation: Past negation: *ne-* on the verb and object in the genitive — *neskaitė knygos* (¶97). Keeping *knygą* accusative is the near-miss; *neskaito* is present.

drills.stem: Complete: **Pernai ____ Kaune.** (Last year we lived in Kaunas.)
drills.explanation: *pernai* marks past narrative: *gyvenome* (¶94, ¶98).

drills.stem: Which are **past** forms?
drills.explanation: *dirba* is present; the others are past (¶93–90).

drills.stem: Which correctly negate in the **past**?
drills.explanation: *ne-* is written onto the verb as one word (¶97). *ne dirbau* is the near-miss.

drills.stem: **Mačiau tave vakar.** Why *mačiau*, not *matau*?
options: Because the third principal part is *matė* (*-ė* type) and 1sg is *-iau*
Because all verbs use *-iau* in every tense
drills.explanation: Dictionary third part *matė* selects *-ė* endings; 1sg softens to *mačiau* (¶93, ¶95).

drills.stem: Complete: **Prieš metus ____ į Lietuvą.** (A year ago I came to Lithuania.)
drills.explanation: Narrative past with *prieš metus*: *atvažiavau* (¶98).

drills.stem: Which pairs show the **same** third-person form for singular and plural in the past?
drills.explanation: Third person is number-indifferent in the past too (¶94 / ¶57). First person changes.

drills.stem: Complete: **Tai ____ geras filmas.** (That was a good film.)
drills.explanation: Past of *būti* in 3rd person: *buvo* (¶96).

drills.stem: A dictionary entry *dirbti, dirba, dirbo* shows how many **principal parts**?
drills.explanation: Three: infinitive, present 3rd, past 3rd. The past stem is not predictable from the other two, so all three are cited.

drills.stem: How many letters in past 1sg **mačiau**?
drills.explanation: Six: m-a-č-i-a-u — the *-ė* type 1sg with *t*→*č* (¶95).

drills.stem: **Ji skaitė knygą** → negate in the past. How many words change form (verb + object)?
drills.explanation: Two: *skaitė*→*neskaitė*, *knygą*→*knygos*. *Ji* unchanged (¶97).

drills.title: Trumpa biografija
drills.passage: Gimiau tūkstantis devyni šimtai devyniasdešimt penktaisiais metais Kaune. Ten gyvenau dešimt metų. Paskui mes atvažiavome į Vilnių, ir aš studijavau universitete. Vakarais dirbau kavinėje ir skaičiau knygas. Pernai nedirbau — buvau namie ir mokiausi lietuvių kalbos. Vakar mačiau seną draugą; mes kalbėjome apie mokyklą. Ji neskaitė mano laiško.
drills.translation: I was born in 1995 in Kaunas. I lived there for ten years. Then we came to Vilnius, and I studied at the university. In the evenings I worked in a café and read books. Last year I did not work — I was at home and studied Lithuanian. Yesterday I saw an old friend; we talked about school. She did not read my letter.

questions.explanation: *Gimiau … Kaune.* Vilnius came later. *Kaune* is locative (¶59).

questions.stem: Which verbs belong to the **-ė** past type?
For how many years did the writer live in Kaunas?
questions.explanation: *gyvenau dešimt metų* — ten, genitive plural after *dešimt* (¶80).

options: Because negation puts the object in the genitive, in the past as in the present.
questions.explanation: Negation-genitive holds in every tense (¶97). Affirmative would be *skaitė mano laišką*.

questions.stem: How many **negated** past-tense verbs appear in the passage?
questions.explanation: Two: *nedirbau* and *neskaitė*. *ne-* is fused to the verb as one word — easy to undercount.
